text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: SEV-2 — routing spillover detected in eu-west-1. Error spike + increased 5xxs for host pools using model-redwood-3b-fallback. See alerts: https://alerts.redwood/SEV4912

alex (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Pulling recent routing metrics and failover logs.

joanne: I'm on standby for traffic steering. tagging @mike for kernel/runtime changes that might affect model compatibility.

samir: Summary from pager: 11:12 UTC sudden increase in route failures from eu-west-1 -> spillover to eu-west-2 and us-west-1; many requests attempted fallback to quantized variant and then 502.

alex (oncall): Immediate mitigation: enabling regional rate dampening and disabling cross-region spillover to non-primary tiers. Executing helm rollout patch for routing-policy service:

```
# snippet: patch to routing-policy config
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap routing-policy --type merge -p '{"data":{"spillover_enabled":"false","max_outbound_per_sec":"200"}}'
```

alex (oncall): Applying now. Will monitor 30s windows.

ops-bot: deploy started by alex (oncall) at 11:18 UTC — rolling update routing-policy/blue -> routing-policy/green (3/3 pods updated)

mike (eng-runtime): Noted. I see increased KV-cache eviction TTLs around the same time in eu-west-1; curious if the fallback path attempted a quantized model variant that lacked proper tokenizer paddings. Pulling runtime logs.

lisa (support): We have 3 inbound tickets mentioning slow responses and errors for EU customers. ETA for initial customer update?

alex (oncall): Will post customer-facing incident banner in 15m after we confirm mitigation effectiveness. For now add to status page: partial degraded performance for EU region endpoints.

joanne: From routing logs (excerpt):
```
2026-02-28T11:12:07Z route-evaluator: host=eu-west-1 pool=model-redwood-3b primary_fail=23 spillover_attempt=1 -> selected eu-west-2
2026-02-28T11:12:08Z proxy: upstream_connect: timeout to eu-west-2:443
2026-02-28T11:12:09Z fallback-decider: fallback_variant=model-redwood-3b-quantized-ptq status=checked
2026-02-28T11:12:09Z lb: request_failed: code=502 reason=invalid_response
```

samir: That 502 looks like incompatibility between quantized kernel output and our post-processing. We saw similar during the last ptq onboarding.

mike (eng-runtime): Confirmed. Kernel logs show tensor-shape mismatch during decode for batch sizes >1 in the quantized path. Root cause hypothesis: recent kernel selector change inadvertently allowed an older quantized kernel for the model variant.

alex (oncall): Action items in-thread:
- alex: keep spillover disabled and monitor traffic (assigned)
- mike: roll back kernel selector change for quantized models in eu-west- (assigned)
- tara (sre): collect full request traces + KV cache hit ratios for 10:50–11:30 window (assigned)
- joanne: prepare timeline and early RCA notes (assigned)

tara (sre): I'm collecting traces now. Running query on trace-store: `service:routing-policy AND env:eu-west-1 AND timestamp:[2026-02-28T10:50 TO 2026-02-28T11:30]` — pulling top 500 slow traces.

mike (eng-runtime): Rolling back kernel selector in eu-west-1 to previous commit c7f8a2 and promoting a canary to eu-west-2 to test fallback path. Command:
```
# rollback kernel selector
git checkout c7f8a2 -- infra/kernel-selector
helm upgrade runtime-kernels -f values-eu-west-1.yaml --namespace runtime --set selectorImage=registry.redwood/c7f8a2
```

ops-bot: rollback job started by mike at 11:29 UTC — progress 1/3 nodes patched

joanne: Timeline so far (short):
- 11:12 UTC: spike in routing errors in eu-west-1; initial spillover to eu-west-2
- 11:14 UTC: failovers to quantized variants result in 502s for batched requests
- 11:18 UTC: feature-flagged spillover disabled; rollout started
- 11:29 UTC: kernel-selector rollback initiated

lisa (support): Customer impact: around ~1400 requests failed for EU customers between 11:12–11:28; some enterprise customers reported latency and increased error rates. Logged impacted accounts: cust-223, cust-889, cust-145 (ticket IDs attached).

samir: Hypotheses to track in RCA:
1) Kernel selector misrouting quantized kernel variant for batched paths -> decode mismatch (mike investigating)
2) KV-cache pressure in primary region increased request latencies causing more spillover (tara investigating metrics)
3) Routing policy thresholds too permissive for short spikes -> cascade (joanne will review thresholds)

alex (oncall): If rollback stabilizes decoders, we'll re-enable controlled spillover with reduced concurrency to test. Otherwise keep it off.

ops-bot: rollout completed at 11:33 UTC — routing-policy pods (3/3) now at new config.

tara (sre): KV-cache hit ratio during spike dropped from 92% -> 61% in eu-west-1, and median latency increased by ~180ms. That supports hypothesis #2.

mike (eng-runtime): Kernel rollback finished at 11:36 UTC on eu-west-1 nodes. Ran a synthetic rerun for batch size 4: decode passed.

alex (oncall): Traffic metrics now: errors trending down to baseline. Re-enabling limited spillover to tier=gold only at 11:45 UTC to validate.

joanne: Adding artifacts to RCA draft in /mnt/rca/SEV4912: logs, traces, timeline, and hypothesis table. Will compile postmortem once we stabilize.

lisa (support): Posting an interim status to customers now. Will include note about degraded performance and that mitigation is in progress.

samir: For the RCA, we should include a short experiment: run fallback synthetic with batch sizes 1..8 across quantized kernel to validate edges. I'll own the test harness.

alex (oncall): Handoff plan: I'm covering the next 30 minutes. If things look stable at 12:15 UTC, I'll close the sev. If anything degrades, page me and tag @sre-rotation.

incident-bot: Incident SEV-2 updated: status=mitigated (partial) at 11:50 UTC. Next update scheduled 12:00 UTC.

joanne: Early RCA notes: preliminary root cause is a combination of kernel-selector regression + transient KV-cache pressure making the routing decision cascade. We'll propose hardening: require kernel-validation gate before selector rollout, and add short-term increase in cache capacity plus revised spillover thresholds.

mike (eng-runtime): Also recommending an automated smoke test that exercises quantized decode on canaries for batch sizes up to 8 before kernel selector rollouts.

alex (oncall): Thanks all. Keep putting artifacts in the RCA folder. I'll prep the customer summary once we have final numbers for failed requests and impacted SLAs.

lisa (support): Updating the tickets with mitigation notes and linking RCA folder.

joanne: I'll start drafting the postmortem and include the timeline above, hypothesis tracking table, and required follow-ups.

alex (oncall): Handoff to tara (sre) at 12:15 UTC unless we get paged.

tara (sre): Taking on-call. Monitoring dashboard up.

ops-bot: incident SEV-2 closed to active paging at 12:20 UTC — status=monitoring.

samir: Adding test plan to the RCA: run 1000 requests across regions with and without KV cache to validate stability.

joanne: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in the RCA thread for writeup.

(End of thread)
